availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Debug your current Claude Code session by reading the session debug log. (bundled)

availableCommands.name: audit
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Parallel exploration of docs, code, config, tests, and specs to identify cruft, then interactive triage with clear action options. (project)

availableCommands.name: codex
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to run Codex CLI (codex exec, codex resume) or wants Codex to review PRs, plans, or specs. Delegates to GPT-5.3-codex with preset reasoning modes. (project)

availableCommands.name: e2e
availableCommands.description: E2E testing patterns for kspec web UI. Use when writing Playwright tests, debugging hydration issues, or working with daemon fixtures. (project)

availableCommands.name: eval-agents
availableCommands.description: Evaluate whether AGENTS.md provides enough context for agents to make correct decisions. Spawns test agents with scenario questions and grades responses. (project)

availableCommands.name: local-review
availableCommands.description: Pre-PR quality review - verify AC coverage, test quality, E2E preference, and test isolation. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Create a pull request from current work. Handles branch creation, commits, push, and PR creation. Detects branch protection and guides through the PR workflow. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr-review
availableCommands.description: Review a PR linked to a kspec task, post findings as inline comments, and merge only when all quality gates pass. You NEVER fix code — you review and comment. If issues found, kick back to worker. (project)

availableCommands.name: release
availableCommands.description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm. (project)

availableCommands.name: svelte-5
availableCommands.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues. (project)

availableCommands.name: create-workflow
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Formalize repeatable patterns into trackable kspec workflows. Design steps, choose triggers, create loop variants, and integrate with skills.

availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Get help with kspec commands and workflows

availableCommands.name: observe
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Capture and act on systemic patterns — friction, successes, questions, and ideas. The feedback loop that drives process improvement.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Translate approved plans into specs and tasks. Import structured documents or create incrementally. Plans persist as durable artifacts with audit trail.

availableCommands.name: reflect
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured reflection at the end of work sessions. Identifies learnings, friction points, and improvements for system evolution.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Kspec-specific review gates — spec alignment, own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, and validation integration. Building block for project-specific review workflows.

availableCommands.name: task-work
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured task lifecycle — start, work, note, submit, complete. Fix cycle handling, scope management, loop mode for automation, and quality gates.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Triage inbox items systematically. Records decisions with audit trail, then executes actions. Supports inbox, observations, and automation eligibility triage.

availableCommands.name: triage-automation
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Assess and prepare tasks for automation eligibility. Verify spec coverage, acceptance criteria, and task readiness for automated agents.

availableCommands.name: triage-inbox
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Process inbox items using the record-act pattern. Categorize, promote to spec/task, merge duplicates, defer, or delete stale items with full audit trail.

availableCommands.name: writing-specs
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Create and maintain specification items — modules, features, requirements, acceptance criteria, and traits. The source of truth for what to build.

availableCommands.name: compact
availableCommands.description: Clear conversation history but keep a summary in context. Optional: /compact [instructions for summarization]

availableCommands.name: context
availableCommands.description: Show current context usage

availableCommands.name: init
availableCommands.description: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

availableCommands.name: pr-comments
availableCommands.description: Get comments from a GitHub pull request

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: Review a pull request

availableCommands.name: security-review
availableCommands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

availableCommands.description: Generate a report analyzing your Claude Code sessions

─── Spec Context ───
Session Stream View
Type: feature
Implementation: in_progress
Description:
  View for watching agent work — both historical and live. Renders structured
  session events (messages, tool calls, thinking blocks) from events.jsonl.
  Live sessions show streaming text with periodic structured refresh.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: A completed session with events.jsonl

    When: The user navigates to /sessions/:id

    Then: The session events render as structured blocks: agent messages (markdown),
tool calls (collapsible with icon, input/output, timing), and thinking blocks
(collapsed by default, expandable)

  [ac-2]
    Given: An active session with streaming output

    When: The user views the session

    Then: Live text streams in real-time via agent_text_chunk WebSocket events,
with periodic structured refresh from events.jsonl

  [ac-3]
    Given: The session stream view

    When: New content arrives while auto-scrolling

    Then: The view auto-scrolls to follow new content, pauses when user scrolls up
(>100px from bottom), and resumes when scrolled back. A "jump to bottom"
button appears when paused.

  [ac-4]
    Given: The session stream view

    When: A session context panel is shown on the left

    Then: It displays session metadata, spec context with AC checklist,
files changed during session, and budget info


─── Notes ───

Perfect! I have successfully read all 13 files from the fix/session-stream-view branch. Here's a summary of what I found:

## Summary of Session Stream Implementation Files

### Components (Svelte)

1. **MessageBlock.svelte** - Renders agent messages as markdown blocks with timestamp and avatar
2. **SessionStream.svelte** - Main stream container with auto-scroll, live streaming text, and jump-to-bottom button
3. **ToolCallView.svelte** - Collapsible tool call blocks showing tool name, input, output, status, and duration
4. **ThinkingBlock.svelte** - Collapsed by default, expandable thinking blocks with brain icon
5. **SystemBlock.svelte** - Horizontal divider blocks for lifecycle events (session start/end, iterations)
6. **SessionContextPanel.svelte** - Right sidebar showing session metadata, spec context with AC checklist, files changed, budget, and timeline
7. **SessionStreamSkeleton.svelte** - Loading skeleton state with shimmer animations

### Utility & Logic

8. **session-utils.ts** - Core parsing and formatting utilities:
   - `parseEventsToBlocks()` - Converts raw events from events.jsonl to structured DisplayBlock types
   - Block type definitions (MessageBlock, ToolCallBlock, ThinkingBlock, SystemBlock)
   - Tool icons and preview extraction
   - Duration/time/age formatting functions
   - `extractFilesChanged()` - Extracts file paths from Write/Edit/NotebookEdit tool calls

### Pages

9. **[id]/+page.svelte** - Session detail page with live streaming via WebSocket:
   - Loads session metadata and events
   - Subscribes to agent events for live text chunks
   - Periodic refresh every 3 seconds
   - Renders context panel + stream

10. **+page.svelte** - Sessions list page:
    - Lists all sessions with status badges, event counts, duration
    - Links to detail view
    - Empty state for no sessions

### API & Backend

11. **api.ts** - Client-side API functions:
    - `fetchSessions()`, `fetchSession()`, `fetchSessionEvents()`
    - Session interface definitions (SessionSummary, SessionDetail, SessionSpecContext, SessionBudget)
    - Supports incremental loading via `since_seq` parameter

12. **sessions.ts** (daemon) - Express routes:
    - `GET /api/sessions` - List all sessions
    - `GET /api/sessions/:id` - Get session detail with spec context and budget
    - `GET /api/sessions/:id/events` - Get events with optional `since_seq` filtering

### Testing

13. **web-ui-session-stream.test.ts** - Comprehensive test suite:
    - Static analysis of Svelte component structure (AC annotations)
    - Unit tests for parseEventsToBlocks, formatDuration, formatTime, extractFilesChanged
    - Tests for all AC coverage areas (ac-1 through ac-4)
    - Animation and accessibility checks

All files are complete and ready for review. The implementation covers the four acceptance criteria:
- **AC-1**: Structured event blocks (message, tool_call, thinking, system)
- **AC-2**: Live streaming via WebSocket with incremental refresh
- **AC-3**: Auto-scroll with jump-to-bottom button
- **AC-4**: Context panel with metadata, spec context, files changed, budget

    "test:shard3": "vitest run --shard=3/3",

    "elysia": "^1.1.31",
    "js-yaml": "^4.1.0",
    "smol-toml": "^1.6.0",
    "ulid": "^2.3.0",
    "yaml": "^2.8.2",
    "zod": "^3.23.8"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@agentclientprotocol/sdk": "^0.14.0",
    "@biomejs/biome": "2.3.11",
    "@tailwindcss/postcss": "^4.1.18",
    "@types/diff": "^7.0.2",
    "@types/js-yaml": "^4.0.9",
    "@types/node": "^20.11.0",
    "autoprefixer": "^10.4.23",
    "clsx": "^2.1.1",
    "postcss": "^8.5.6",
    "shx": "^0.4.0",
    "tailwind-merge": "^3.4.0",
    "tailwind-variants": "^3.2.2",
    "tailwindcss": "^4.1.18",
    "tsx": "^4.7.0",
    "typescript": "^5.3.3",
    "vitest": "^4.0.17"
  },
  "files": [
    "dist",
    "templates",
    "plugin"
  ],
  "keywords": [
    "specification",
    "requirements",
    "yaml",
    "cli",
    "ai",
    "agent"
  ],
  "license": "MIT"
}

## File Contents Summary

### 1. **session-utils.ts**
Utility functions for parsing session events into structured display blocks. Key exports include:
- `BlockType` union of `'message' | 'tool_call' | 'tool_result' | 'thinking' | 'system'`
- Interfaces: `MessageBlock`, `ToolCallBlock`, `ThinkingBlock`, `SystemBlock`, `DisplayBlock`
- `getToolIcon()` - maps tool names to emoji icons
- `getToolInputPreview()` - extracts short previews from tool input
- `parseEventsToBlocks()` - main parser converting `SessionEvent[]` to `DisplayBlock[]`
- Formatting utilities: `formatDuration()`, `formatTime()`, `formatElapsed()`, `formatAge()`
- `extractFilesChanged()` - extracts file paths from Write/Edit/NotebookEdit tool calls

### 2. **SessionStream.svelte**
Main stream display component. Features:
- Renders `DisplayBlock[]` as structured components (MessageBlock, ToolCallView, ThinkingBlock, SystemBlock)
- Auto-scroll behavior with 100px threshold for user override
- "Jump to bottom" button visible when user scrolls up
- Live streaming text display with blinking cursor
- Empty state messaging
- `aria-live="polite"` for accessibility
- Smooth scroll behavior with `requestAnimationFrame`

### 3. **SessionContextPanel.svelte**
Right sidebar with session context. Sections:
- Session metadata (status, agent type, duration, trigger)
- Spec context with AC checklist (when available)
- Stats grid (events, iterations, tasks completed, session type)
- Budget info (tasks started vs max per cycle with progress bar)
- Files changed section (shortened paths showing last 2 segments)
- Timeline (started, ended, duration in relative format)

### 4. **+page.svelte** (route: `/sessions/[id]`)
Main page component orchestrating the session view. Key logic:
- Loads session metadata and events on mount
- WebSocket listeners for `agent_text_chunk` and `agent_invocation` events
- Periodic refresh every 3 seconds for live sessions
- Handles streaming text accumulation and display
- Two-column layout: SessionContextPanel + SessionStream
- Loading skeleton during initial fetch
- Error state display

### 5. **ToolCallView.svelte**
Tool call block renderer with:
- Collapsible header showing tool icon, name, preview, status icon, and duration
- Expanded view with formatted Input/Output JSON
- Color-coded borders by status (completed=green, failed=red, running=yellow)
- "Show full output" button for truncated outputs >1000 chars
- Running state animation (spinning loader)
- Timestamp display

### 6. **ThinkingBlock.svelte**
Thinking block renderer with:
- Collapsible header (collapsed by default)
- Brain icon and "Thinking" label
- 80-char preview when collapsed
- Full monospace content when expanded
- Light border styling with `border-l-design-ring`

All files are fully linked together and implement the session stream viewing feature with live streaming support, auto-scroll, expandable sections, and comprehensive context display.

The project uses **three distinct testing patterns**:

#### A. **Static Source Analysis Tests** (vitest)
- Location: `/tests/*.test.ts`
- Pattern: Read source files and verify string patterns
- Examples: `web-ui-app-shell.test.ts`, `web-ui-design-system.test.ts`
- Use case: Verify file structure, configuration, and compiled output
- **No runtime dependencies** - these are pure file inspections

#### B. **Unit Tests** (vitest)
- Location: `packages/web-ui/tests/board-utils.test.ts`, `packages/shared/tests/types.test.ts`
- Pattern: Pure function testing with test fixtures
- Use case: Business logic validation (distribution, formatting, type checking)
- Example: `distributeToColumns()`, `formatAge()`, `getStatusClasses()`

#### C. **E2E Tests** (Playwright)
- Location: `packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/*.spec.ts`
- Pattern: Full daemon + browser integration
- Use case: API contracts, WebSocket protocols, UI interactions
- Architecture: Test-managed daemon fixture with `.kspec` simulation

---

### 2. **Web UI Testing Setup**

**Package.json** (`packages/web-ui/package.json`):
- **No `@testing-library/svelte`** installed
- **No Svelte component unit testing** framework
- Testing tools available:
  - `@playwright/test` for E2E
  - `vitest` for utilities/unit tests (run from root)

**Test Configuration**:
- Root `vitest.config.ts`:
  - `environment: 'node'`
  - Global setup in `tests/global-setup.ts`
  - Excludes E2E: `'**/packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/**'`

- Playwright config (`packages/web-ui/playwright.config.ts`):
  - Workers: 1 (daemon on fixed port 3456)
  - baseURL: `http://localhost:3456`
  - Daemon started by test fixture (not webServer)

---

### 3. **Session Test Patterns** (CLI tests)

Location: `tests/cli/session-*.test.ts`

**Key characteristics**:
```typescript
// Uses setupTempFixtures() + kspecJson<T>() helpers
beforeEach(async () => {
  tempDir = await setupTempFixtures();
  initGitRepo(tempDir);
});

const session = kspecJson<SessionContext>('session start --json', tempDir);
expect(session.ready_tasks.length).toBe(5);
```

**Type-safe JSON parsing**:
- Uses shared type definitions in `tests/helpers/session-types.ts`
- All SessionContext fields are optional (flexible subset testing)
- Types mirror source in `src/cli/commands/session/types.ts`

**Common helpers**:
- `setupTempFixtures()` — copy pre-built fixtures
- `createTempDir()` — empty temp project
- `initGitRepo()` — git setup with test config
- `kspec()` — run CLI, return result
- `kspecJson<T>()` — run with `--json`, parse typed response
- `git()` — wrapper for git commands

---

### 4. **E2E Test Patterns** (WebSocket, API, UI)

**Test Base Fixture** (`packages/web-ui/tests/fixtures/test-base.ts`):
```typescript
export const test = base.extend<{ daemon: DaemonFixture }>({
  daemon: async ({}, use) => {
    // 1. Kill existing daemon on port 3456
    // 2. Create temp .kspec with fixtures
    // 3. Simulate shadow worktree (.git file + metadata)
    // 4. Start daemon with kspec serve start --daemon
    // 5. Poll health endpoint until ready
    // 6. Provide fixture with tempDir, kspecDir, createSecondProject()
    // 7. Cleanup on test end
  }
});
```

**Key points**:
- Fixture creates **realistic shadow branch simulation**
- Bun runtime required (checked during fixture setup)
- Web UI build verified before starting daemon
- Multi-project support via `createSecondProject()`

**E2E Test Examples**:

```typescript
// api-websocket.spec.ts
test('subscribes to topic and receives broadcasts', async ({ page }) => {
  const ws = await connectWebSocket(page);
  await sendCommand(page, { action: 'subscribe', payload: { topics: ['tasks'] } });
  const broadcast = await waitForBroadcast(page, 'tasks', 5000);
  expect(broadcast.data).toBeDefined();
});

// api-tasks.spec.ts
test('filters tasks by multiple status values', async ({ request }) => {
  const response = await request.get(`${DAEMON_URL}/api/tasks?status=pending&status=in_progress`);
  expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
  const body = await response.json();

```

### 5. **Testing Best Practices in This Project**

**AC Coverage Annotations** (machine-parseable):

```javascript
  // AC coverage verification in test registry

```

**Test Isolation** (`packages/web-ui/tests/fixtures/project-tests/coverage-test.test.ts`):
- Fixtures are **separate from unit tests**
- E2E fixtures in `packages/web-ui/tests/fixtures/`
- Unit test fixtures in `packages/shared/tests/fixtures/`

**ULID Validity** (critical!):
- Crockford base32: excludes I, L, O, U
- Use `testUlid(prefix)` helper for valid test ULIDs
- Silent test failures if invalid ULIDs used

**Multiline tests**:

- Full suite required before PR
